trajectory_summary: This is an efficient, cooperative qualifying call with a genuinely strong lead ($1,100-$1,300/month bill) that gets muddied by weak time-anchoring during scheduling. The rep ran verify and bill-collection cleanly and fast, but the appointment-setting stretch (05:14-07:53) turned into an avoidable multi-round negotiation because the rep never stated a firm duration upfront.

observed_outcome.quote: Sounds good. I'll just get you down from Monday, the twentieth, at 09:30.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day and time (Monday the 20th at 9:30) is locked, the bill was received on-call, and a confirmation email was promised — this is a solid booked outcome, though the wife (confirmed co-owner) was never explicitly included in the appointment.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep reacts with surprise ('Oh, wow. Really? It's that high?') and briefly validates the customer's solar interest, but never flips the number into an explicit reason to act now — the flip should have landed at 02:39-02:45 where the rep instead moves straight into pitch mechanics.

bill_document_audit.ask_quote: Do you typically get your electric bills in the mail or online?
bill_document_audit.reasoning: Rep asked how the customer receives bills, offered text or email, sent the customer a link/prompt via email, and the customer successfully emailed the bill back before the call ended, confirmed by the rep at 09:49 ('Perfect. Just got it.').

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep asked the interest question early and got a clear bill-pain reason, but never explicitly tied the appointment or the bill discussion back to 'energy costs' as the customer's stated motivator — the closest moment (02:39-02:45) validates generically rather than reinforcing the customer's own words.

What got you interested in looking at solar for your home?
Well, I just wanted to start by confirming this address that we have here.
Is there anyone else on the title besides you, Reginald?
Is that a metal roof on the home?
And then do you know who you're currently doing your electricity with here, Reginald?
And about how much are you guys paying for electricity right now on average?
And so all that's needed to, qualify is just a credit score above 670.
Do you typically get your electric bills in the mail or online?
Sounds good. I'll just get you down from Monday, the twentieth, at 09:30.

script_coverage.quote: I'll just send you a confirmation email with the date and time of the meeting back so you have it in writing.

attempt_quotes: We do have Friday at 09:30 and then Saturday at 9AM.
Would it, make more sense to do next Thursday, or even, like, Wednesday at 09:30?
So we have for 09:30, we have Monday, Wednesday, or Friday where we can do 09:30.
objections.reasoning: The customer cycled through several unavailable days/times due to a packed schedule; the rep kept offering alternates until the customer landed on Monday the 20th at 9:30, which they accepted.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Firm time-anchoring before offering appointment slots
primary_coaching_focus.quote: How how long how long how long are you gonna be here?
primary_coaching_focus.why: The schema is explicit that vague time framing correlates with no-shows (protocols.time_constraint). This rep had no ready anchor line when the customer pushed back on duration, producing a visible stumble and five extra minutes of back-and-forth before a date locked — all avoidable with a scripted 'It's a 30-minute call' opener before offering days.

key_moments.stewart_read: An unusually high bill figure is captured, but the rep's response is limited to surprise rather than a flip into emotional alignment-against-the-utility.

key_moments.quote: Gotcha. I mean, I could definitely see where you're looking into, to solar.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer just gave the single strongest anchor of the call (a bill in the $1,100-$1,300 range) and the rep validates generically instead of flipping it into urgency against the utility.

key_moments.quote: How how long how long how long are you gonna be here?
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep never anchored appointment length confidently before this point ('It's a 30-minute call — we'll get you in and out' per schema) and instead scrambles reactively once the customer states a hard 30-minute ceiling, producing an audible stumble.
Customer identifies a co-owner on the title, but the rep never circles back to confirm she'll be included on the appointment.
